trust_decision.summary: Whether the user-supplied ?next= value is a same-site URL safe to redirect to, decided (after the fix) in each of the four vendored django-notifications action views right before redirect(_next); at the pinned commit there is no check at all.

landing_point.why: Advisory title names the notification endpoints and the next parameter; mark_all_as_read is the first redirect(_next) in notifications/views.py, and all four sites sit in that one file.

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: All four fix sites are sibling functions in notifications/views.py (fix.diff:31-64); no second implementation, lower-level API or wrapper is touched.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: For the O8 Referer-based redirects: 'the advisory is about the next query parameter on notification endpoints; Referer is a browser-set header in other apps (offboarding, outlook_auth, payroll), not attacker-chosen input'.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A legitimate relative/same-host ?next= (e.g. back to the page the user came from) must still redirect there; only an absent/unsafe next falls back to notifications:unread / notifications:all. Over-broad fixes that drop next entirely, or the published fix as written (it reads ALLOWED_HOSTS from the notifications.settings module, which does not define it), break this.

O6_input_shapes: scheme-relative //other and backslash variants, handled by Django's url_has_allowed_host_and_scheme
non-http schemes (javascript:) rejected by the same helper

O7_producer.where: next comes straight from request.GET at each site (notifications/views.py:72,88,105,127)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Offboarding permission/feature decorators write the raw Referer into a window.location script response with no host check
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Referer header, not the next parameter; other app; looks like a permission-denied UX path

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Outlook token refresh redirects to the raw Referer
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Referer, admin-only permission_required view, OAuth integration app

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Tax bracket delete falls back to redirecting to the raw Referer
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Referer, error-only fallback branch in payroll

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a next-driven redirect in a non-JSON variant of the live_* API views or a mark_all_as_unread view
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Upstream django-notifications shape; the vendored app already repeats the _next idiom four times.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Horilla's own mark_as_read_notification honouring ?next= instead of the htmx span
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Second notification implementation in another package doing the same job; a maintainer adding non-htmx support would copy the vendored _next idiom.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: login next check followed by a query-string append, which is a parser-differential (how-type) spot if the check ran on a different string than the one redirected
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The code already concatenates params after validating next_url.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Wrap the four redirect(_next) calls with url_has_allowed_host_and_scheme (or use the existing HorillaRedirect from horilla/http/response.py:6-39); one edit pattern in one file closes everything the report describes.

out_of_scope_notes: Published fix appears broken: notifications/views.py:18 binds `settings` to notifications.settings, which defines no ALLOWED_HOSTS (notifications/settings.py:4-20), so fix.diff:31 etc. would raise AttributeError whenever next is set; hidden tests must not mirror it.
base/views.py:5099-5105 and base/views.py:5083-5095 mark/delete notifications by id without a recipient check (IDOR, not this advisory).
offboarding/decorators.py:42 interpolates Referer into a script tag (possible XSS, separate weakness).
unverified: Whether Referer-based redirects count under this advisory's property is a judgement call; the project itself treats them as open-redirect risk at horilla/methods.py:88-94 and helpdesk/views.py:1489-1495.
Runtime behaviour of the published fix (AttributeError) inferred from reading, not executed.
